question_en: Which Ethiopian runner won the 1960 Olympic marathon while running barefoot?
explanation_en: Abebe Bikila won in Rome and became the first Black African Olympic gold medalist.

question_en: How many months are in the Ethiopian calendar?
explanation_en: It has twelve 30-day months plus a short thirteenth month called Pagumen.

question_en: What does the name Addis Ababa mean in Amharic?
explanation_en: Addis Ababa translates literally as New Flower.

question_en: What grain is traditionally used to make injera?
explanation_en: Teff is a tiny cereal grain native to the Horn of Africa and the traditional base for injera.

question_en: The famous churches of Lalibela were carved primarily from what?
explanation_en: The eleven medieval churches were hewn downward from monolithic rock.

question_en: How many hearts does an octopus have?
explanation_en: Two hearts pump blood to the gills and one pumps it around the body.

question_en: Which animal is famous for producing cube-shaped droppings?
explanation_en: Wombat intestines shape the material into cubes before it leaves the body.

question_en: What color is a polar bear's skin beneath its fur?
explanation_en: Polar bears have black skin beneath translucent, light-scattering fur.

question_en: What is a group of flamingos commonly called?
explanation_en: Flamboyance is the best-known collective noun for a group of flamingos.

question_en: Which mammal has fingerprints so similar to humans that they can look alike under a microscope?
explanation_en: Koalas developed distinctive fingerprints independently of primates.

question_en: On which planet is one full rotation longer than one trip around the Sun?
explanation_en: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate but about 225 days to orbit the Sun.

question_en: What was the subject of the world's first webcam?
explanation_en: Cambridge researchers aimed a camera at the Trojan Room coffee pot to see whether it was full.

question_en: What is the name for the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape?
explanation_en: The event horizon marks the point beyond which even light cannot return.

question_en: Which metal is liquid at ordinary room temperature?
explanation_en: Mercury is the only metallic element that is liquid under standard room conditions.

question_en: What is the largest desert on Earth?
explanation_en: A desert is defined by low precipitation, making Antarctica the world's largest.

question_en: Which sea has no land coastline?
explanation_en: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by ocean currents rather than land.

question_en: What is the capital city of Australia?
explanation_en: Canberra was selected as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

question_en: Which country has three capital cities?
explanation_en: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein divide the executive, legislative and judicial roles.

question_en: The shortest recorded war, fought in 1896, lasted less than an hour between Britain and which sultanate?
explanation_en: The Anglo-Zanzibar War ended in roughly 40 minutes.

question_en: What household object did ancient Romans collect urine to help clean?
explanation_en: Roman fullers used ammonia from urine in laundering fabric.

question_en: Which board game began as 'The Landlord's Game'?
explanation_en: Elizabeth Magie's Landlord's Game was the key predecessor of Monopoly.

question_en: What food container held some of the ashes of the inventor of the Pringles can?
explanation_en: Fred Baur requested that part of his cremated remains be buried in his invention.

question_en: Botanically, what type of plant food is a peanut?
explanation_en: Peanuts grow in pods and belong to the legume family, like beans and peas.

question_en: Vanilla flavoring comes from the fruit of what type of flowering plant?
explanation_en: Vanilla pods are the fruit of climbing orchids in the genus Vanilla.

question_en: Which part of the cashew fruit grows outside the fleshy cashew apple?
explanation_en: The cashew seed sits inside a shell attached beneath the cashew apple.

question_en: Which citrus fruit is used to flavor traditional Earl Grey tea?
explanation_en: Earl Grey is scented with oil from bergamot citrus peel.

question_en: What is the name of the dot over a lowercase i or j?
explanation_en: Tittle is the typographic name for that small distinguishing mark.

question_en: The word 'robot' comes from a Czech word meaning what kind of work?
explanation_en: Robot derives from robota, meaning forced labor or drudgery.

question_en: What is the symbol '&' called?
explanation_en: The ampersand is a logogram representing the word 'and'.

question_en: What do you call a word that reads the same forward and backward?
explanation_en: Examples include level, civic and radar.

question_en: How many rock-hewn churches make up the famous Lalibela group?
explanation_en: UNESCO recognizes a group of eleven churches.

question_en: Which isolated Lalibela church has a cross-shaped plan?
explanation_en: The church of Saint George stands apart from the main groups.

question_en: What shape are the traditional Lasta tukul houses near Lalibela?
explanation_en: The local houses have circular plans and two storeys.

question_en: How many monuments does UNESCO describe at the archaeological site of Tiya?
explanation_en: The listed group includes 32 carved stelae.

question_en: Which weapons appear as carvings on many of the Tiya stelae?
explanation_en: Sword shapes occur alongside other symbols.

question_en: What material is used for the human-shaped memorial statues in Konso?
explanation_en: The carved figures honor people and memorable deeds.

question_en: What holds the agricultural terraces of Konso in place?
explanation_en: Communities built these terraces for farming in a dry landscape.

question_en: How many mosques are recorded in UNESCO’s description of Harar Jugol?
explanation_en: UNESCO also records 102 shrines in the historic town.

question_en: How many historic gates originally divided Harar Jugol into neighborhoods?
explanation_en: The gates corresponded to the main roads into town.

question_en: About how long is the largest fallen obelisk at Aksum?
explanation_en: Its enormous carved stone lies where it fell.

question_en: Alongside Greek and Sabaean, which Ethiopian language appears in King Ezana’s trilingual inscriptions?
explanation_en: The three scripts record royal texts from ancient Aksum.

question_en: Which emperor and his successors used Fasil Ghebbi in Gondar as their royal residence?
explanation_en: The enclosure contains palaces and other royal buildings.

question_en: How many Earth days does Mercury need to circle the Sun?
explanation_en: Its short orbit gives it a very brief year.

question_en: A full sunrise-to-sunrise day on Mercury lasts about how many Earth days?
explanation_en: Its rotation and orbit combine to produce a very long solar day.

question_en: How many natural moons does Mercury have?
explanation_en: Mercury has no natural satellites.

question_en: Mercury is named after a swift god from which ancient civilization?
explanation_en: The name refers to the fast-moving Roman messenger god.

question_en: What acid makes up the dense clouds of Venus?
explanation_en: The clouds sit above an extremely hot surface.

question_en: Which gas makes up most of Venus’s atmosphere?
explanation_en: The dense atmosphere traps a huge amount of heat.

question_en: Which planet is hotter at its surface than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun?
explanation_en: Its dense atmosphere produces an extreme greenhouse effect.

question_en: Which metal’s rust gives Mars much of its reddish appearance?
explanation_en: Iron-bearing material oxidizes in the rocks and dust.

question_en: What are the two small moons of Mars called?
explanation_en: Both are irregularly shaped natural satellites.

question_en: What is the name of the enormous volcano on Mars?
explanation_en: It is the largest volcano in the solar system.

question_en: What do you call a sentence that uses every letter of an alphabet?
explanation_en: Pangrams are often used to demonstrate typefaces.

question_en: What is made by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase?
explanation_en: The same letters are used in a new order.

question_en: What is the term for words such as hiss and buzz that imitate sounds?
explanation_en: The word’s sound resembles what it describes.

question_en: What kind of word blends parts of two words, as in brunch?
explanation_en: Parts of two meanings and spellings combine.

question_en: What do you call two words that sound alike but have different meanings?
explanation_en: Their spelling can differ even when their pronunciation matches.

question_en: What is the study of where words come from called?
explanation_en: It traces a word’s history and development.

question_en: What do you call an abbreviation such as NASA that is pronounced as a word?
explanation_en: Initial letters form a pronounceable new word.

question_en: What is the term for a word with the opposite meaning of another?
explanation_en: Hot and cold are a simple example.

question_en: Which part of a cinnamon tree becomes the spice in your kitchen?
explanation_en: Strips of the fragrant inner bark are dried.

question_en: Cloves are dried unopened parts of what structure on a tree?
explanation_en: The buds are harvested before the flowers open.

question_en: Nutmeg and mace come from the same fruit. Which part becomes nutmeg?
explanation_en: Mace is the covering around that seed.

question_en: What is the spice made from the covering around a nutmeg seed called?
explanation_en: The covering is known botanically as an aril.

question_en: Peppercorns are dried examples of which plant part?
explanation_en: Black pepper comes from the fruit of a climbing plant.

question_en: Despite its name, allspice is made from what rather than a spice mixture?
explanation_en: A single plant supplies the berries used for allspice.

question_en: What part of the saffron crocus becomes the costly red spice?
explanation_en: The flower’s small stigmas are collected and dried.

question_en: The edible part of ginger is an underground stem known as what?
explanation_en: It is a stem structure rather than a true root.

question_en: What color is the blood of an octopus?
explanation_en: Its oxygen-carrying system uses copper.

question_en: Which metal helps octopus blood transport oxygen?
explanation_en: The copper-containing molecule is called hemocyanin.

question_en: What hard mouthpart does an octopus use to bite its food?
explanation_en: The mouth has a hard beak inside the ring of arms.

question_en: Octopuses can move by jet propulsion. What do they expel?
explanation_en: Pushing water through a siphon moves the animal.

question_en: Despite looking like underwater plants, corals belong to which kingdom?
explanation_en: Coral colonies are built from many tiny animals.

question_en: What are the tiny individual animals that form coral colonies called?
explanation_en: Many polyps together form what we call a coral colony.

question_en: Which river pours over Victoria Falls?
explanation_en: The falls cut across this river in southern Africa.

question_en: Victoria Falls lies between Zambia and which other country?
explanation_en: The World Heritage property spans both countries.

question_en: What volcanic rock forms the gorges around Victoria Falls?
explanation_en: The river has cut through layers of ancient lava.

question_en: Lamu’s historic Swahili old town is in which country?
explanation_en: The island settlement lies on the East African coast.

question_en: Alongside mangrove timber, what marine-derived building material characterizes old Lamu?
explanation_en: Local buildings use stone formed from coral.

question_en: What is the deepest named place in the ocean called?
explanation_en: It lies in the western Pacific’s Mariana Trench.
